model: Case B: seller control with unavailable submitted evidence
scope: Finite-horizon control with fixed upfront revenue, not a market equilibrium or welfare ranking.
timing: Task obligation registered; seller knows policy, rho, epsilon and remaining horizon.
Seller receives current reputation-dependent revenue and chooses effort.
Seller privately observes actual task success or failure and chooses report or withhold.
A submitted truthful certificate is independently lost with probability epsilon.
The independent monitoring draw is revealed only after effort and reporting; reputation is updated.
information: The seller cannot condition effort or reporting on the realized monitoring or delivery-loss draws.
certificate_accuracy: Every received certificate is truthful. There are no false certificates; epsilon changes availability only.

rules.STRICT: If monitored, received success sets G; received failure or missing evidence sets B. If unmonitored, state holds.
rules.HOLD: If monitored, received success sets G and received failure sets B; missing evidence holds the prior state. If unmonitored, state holds.

arithmetic: Exact rational arithmetic for both production backward recursion and the independent exhaustive oracle.
limitations: Evidence loss is exogenous, independent and identically distributed; no outcome-dependent outages or strategic delivery sabotage.
Audit and evidence-production costs, buyer participation, price adjustment, seller exit and identity reset are not modeled.
An adverse update after successful submitted evidence is lost is measured separately from an actual G-to-B downgrade.
Certificate and reporting counts use the stated tie convention; effort and success do not establish market welfare.
A finite horizon with upfront revenue provides no terminal effort incentive.
The hypothetical rules are not attributed to any deployed protocol.
